html:
Scipio Africanus was the Roman general who won the Second Punic War, beating Hannibal at the Battle of Zama in 202 BCE. He lived from 236 or 235 to about 183 BCE.

He came from one of Rome's great families and survived the disaster at Cannae as a young officer. In 210 BCE, at only about 25 and after his father and uncle had been killed there, he was given command in Spain. He took the main Carthaginian base, New Carthage, in 209 BCE and drove Carthage out of Spain by 206 BCE.

He then argued, against older senators, for carrying the war to Africa. He landed in 204 BCE, forced Carthage to recall Hannibal from Italy, and won at Zama. The name Africanus honoured the victory.

He served as consul and censor and went east with his brother Lucius against the Seleucid king Antiochus III. Back in Rome, his enemies, with Cato the Elder behind them, attacked the brothers in court over money. Bitter, Scipio retired to his country estate and died there. His daughter was Cornelia, mother of the Gracchi.
sum: Scipio Africanus was the Roman general who won the Second Punic War, beating Hannibal at the Battle of Zama in 202 BCE. He lived from 236 or 235 to about 183 BCE.
